fix(scanf): the engine was pruned because only the BACKEND names it

`sscanf()` and `fscanf()` do not compile. Any form, any program:

    $r = sscanf("alice 30", "%s %d");
    → EIR backend error: call to unknown function __elephc_scanf

Both lower to a call into the scanf prelude, whose functions no PHP source ever names — the name
appears only inside the lowering, as a Rust string constant. The declaration-reachability pass
walks PHP, finds nothing pointing at `__elephc_scanf`, and prunes it. The call survives; the body
does not. There is no diagnostic anywhere near the cause: the failure surfaces in the backend, one
pass later, as a missing symbol.

The prelude is injected only when the program references `sscanf`/`fscanf`, so its presence in the
inventory is ALREADY the proof that the program needs every function in it. Recording the group and
forcing it costs nothing in pay-for-use terms and makes the pass agree with the lowering.

THREE injection sites had to move together — `pipeline.rs`, `tests/codegen/support/compiler.rs` and
`src/ir_lower/tests/mod.rs` — and the codegen harness needed more than the new argument: it passed
an EMPTY forced-group set, so the rule would have had nowhere to apply and every fixture would have
kept failing while the real compiler built the same program.

The surface was swept rather than the one name fixed. Fifteen builtins that lower into an injected
prelude were compiled and diffed against `php -n`: `hash_init`/`hash_update`/`hash_final`,
`hash_copy`, `mktime`, `gmmktime`, `var_export`, `gzencode`, `dir()`, `array_is_list`,
`get_object_vars`, `is_callable`, `str_getcsv`, `fgetcsv`. Only these two were broken, and the
reason the others are safe is worth recording: their PHP-visible names ARE written in user source,
and the primitives beneath them — `__elephc_hash_ctx_init` and its family — are registered
BUILTINS, not prelude PHP. The scanf engine is the only body reachable purely through an emitted
call.

STILL DIVERGENT, found by the same sweep and not fixed here: `gzopen("php://memory", "wb")` warns
`fopen(php://memory): Failed to open stream` where php warns `gzopen(): Cannot represent a stream
of type MEMORY as a File Descriptor` and both answer `false`.

`io::streams` goes from 11 failures to 7.
EOF
